Package org.bsc.langgraph4j.utils

Interface ExceptionUtils

public interface ExceptionUtils
Stateless helpers for inspecting and unwrapping exception cause chains.

All methods are static, side-effect free and thread-safe.

  • Method Details

    • getRootCause

      static Throwable getRootCause(Throwable throwable)
      Returns the root cause of the given throwable, i.e. the last element of its cause chain.
      Parameters:
      throwable - the throwable to inspect; must not be null
      Returns:
      the deepest cause, or throwable itself if it has no cause
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if throwable is null

    • findCauseByType

      static <Ex extends Throwable> Optional<Ex> findCauseByType(Throwable throwable, Class<Ex> type)
      Searches the cause chain (starting from throwable itself) for a throwable of the given type.

      The match is on the exact class (getClass().equals(type)), so subclasses of type are not matched. If several elements match, the deepest one is returned.

      Type Parameters:
      Ex - the exception type
      Parameters:
      throwable - the head of the cause chain; if null the result is empty
      type - the exact exception class to look for
      Returns:
      the deepest matching cause, or an empty Optional if none matches

    • isWrapper

      static boolean isWrapper(Throwable e)
      Tells whether the given throwable is a generic wrapper that can be unwrapped.
      Parameters:
      e - the throwable to test; must not be null
      Returns:
      true if e is an InvocationTargetException, CompletionException or ExecutionException and has a non-null cause
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if e is null
      See Also:
      • unwrap(Throwable)

    • unwrap

      static Throwable unwrap(@NonNull Throwable e)
      Strips generic wrapper exceptions to expose the meaningful underlying cause.

      Walks the cause chain while isWrapper(Throwable) holds and keeps the last element produced by that walk. Note that the walk only emits throwables that are themselves wrappers, so the result is the innermost wrapper (the one whose cause is not a wrapper), not that wrapper's cause.

      Parameters:
      e - the throwable to unwrap; if null or not a wrapper it is returned as is
      Returns:
      the innermost wrapper in the chain, or e if it is not a wrapper
      See Also:
      • isWrapper(Throwable)
